def-image.title: Image
def-image.html:
Let \(f: V \to W\) be a linear transformation. Define the image of \(f\) by \[ \im (f) \coloneqq \left\{ \w \in W : \w = f(\v) \text{ for some } \v \in V \right\}. \]

i.e. The image contains all the possible outputs of the function \(f\).

def-kernel.title: Kernel
def-kernel.html:
Let \(f: V \to W\) be a linear transformation. Define the kernel of \(f\) by \[ \ker (f) \coloneqq \left\{ \v \in V : f(\v) = \mathbf{0}_W \right\}. \]

i.e. The kernel contains everything in the domain that becomes the zero vector under \(f\).

def-linear-transformation.title: Linear Transformation
def-linear-transformation.html:
Let \(V, W\) be vector spaces over \(F\). A function \(T : V \to W\) is called a linear transformation (or linear map), if

  1. \(T(\v_1 + \v_2) = T(\v_1) + T(\v_2)\), for all \(\v_1, \v_2 \in V\);
  2. \(T(\lambda \v) = \lambda T(\v)\), for all \(\lambda \in F\) and \(\v \in V\).

def-nullity.title: Nullity
def-nullity.html: Let \(f : V \to W\) be a linear transformation. The nullity of \(f\) is defined by \[ \nullity(f) \coloneqq \dim (\ker (f)). \]

def-rank.title: Rank
def-rank.html: Let \(f : V \to W\) be a linear transformation. The rank of \(f\) is defined by \[ \rank(f) \coloneqq \dim (\im (f)). \]

exm-complex-conjugation.title: Complex Conjugation
exm-complex-conjugation.html: Determine whether complex conjugation \(T : \nC \to \nC\) defined by \(T(z) = \overline{z}\), where \(\overline{a + bi} = a - bi\), is a linear transformation.

exm-constant-function.title: Constant Function
exm-constant-function.html: Determine whether \(T : \nR \to \nR\) defined by \(T(x) = 5\) for all \(x \in \nR\) is a linear transformation.

exm-coordinate-transformation.title: A Specific Matrix Transformation
exm-coordinate-transformation.html: Determine whether \(T : F^3 \to F^2\) defined by \(T(a_1, a_2, a_3) = (2a_1 + a_3, \; a_2 - a_1)\) is a linear transformation.

exm-deter.html: Is it possible to have a linear map \(f: \nR^2 \to \nR^3\) such that \[ f(1, 0) = (2, 3, 4), \quad f(1, 1) = (3, 4, 5), \quad f(2, 3) = (4, 5 6)? \]

exm-deter-two.html: Suppose we are give a linear transformation \(f: \nR[x]_{\leq 3} \to \nR[x]_{\leq 2}\). And it is also know that \[ f(x^3) = 3x^2, \quad f(x^2) = 2x, \quad f(x) = 1, \quad f(1)= 0. \]

exm-differentiation.title: Differentiation
exm-differentiation.html: Determine whether \(D : \nR[x] \to \nR[x]\) defined by \(D(f(x)) = f'(x)\) (the derivative) is a linear transformation.

exm-differentiation-kernel-image.title: Differentiation
exm-differentiation-kernel-image.html: Let \(D : \nR[x]_{\leq 3} \to \nR[x]_{\leq 2}\) be defined by \(D(f(x)) = f'(x)\). Find the kernel and image of \(D\).

exm-identity.title: Identity Map
exm-identity.html: Let \(V\) be a vector space. Determine whether the identity map \(\id_V : V \to V\) defined by \(\id_V(\v) = \v\) is a linear transformation.

exm-inclusion.title: Inclusion Map
exm-inclusion.html: Let \(W \subseteq V\) be a subspace. Determine whether the inclusion map \(\iota : W \hookrightarrow V\) defined by \(\iota(\w) = \w\) is a linear transformation.

exm-integration.title: Integration
exm-integration.html: Determine whether \(T : \nR[x] \to \nR[x]\) defined by \(T(f(x)) = \int_0^x f(t) \, \dd t\) is a linear transformation.

exm-matrix-composition.title: Composition Operator
exm-matrix-composition.html: Fix a continuous function \(g : \nR \to \nR\). Determine whether the composition operator \(C_g : C(\nR) \to C(\nR)\) defined by \(C_g(f) = f \circ g\), i.e., \(C_g(f)(x) = f(g(x))\), is a linear transformation.

exm-matrix-transformation.title: Left Multiplication by a Matrix
exm-matrix-transformation.html: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) be an \(m \times n\) matrix. Determine whether \(f_\A : F^n \to F^m\) defined by \(f_\A(\v) = \A\v\) (where \(\v\) is viewed as a column vector) is a linear transformation.

exm-multiplication-by-x.title: Multiplication by x
exm-multiplication-by-x.html: Determine whether \(T : F[x] \to F[x]\) defined by \(T(f(x)) = x \cdot f(x)\) is a linear transformation.

exm-norm.title: Norm
exm-norm.html: Determine whether \(T : \nR^n \to \nR\) defined by \(T(\v) = \|\v\|\) (the Euclidean norm) is a linear transformation.

exm-nullity-rank-diff.html: Recall that for \(D : \nR[x]_{\leq 3} \to \nR[x]_{\leq 2}\) defined by \[ D(f(x)) = f'(x), \] we have \(\ker(D) = \nR\) and \(\im (D) = \nR[x]_{\leq 2}\). Compute the nullity and rank of \(D\).

exm-projection.title: Projection onto a Coordinate Axis
exm-projection.html: Determine whether \(T : \nR^2 \to \nR^2\) defined by \(T(a_1, a_2) = (a_1, 0)\) is a linear transformation.

exm-rotation.title: Rotation in the Plane
exm-rotation.html: Determine whether rotation by angle \(\theta\) (counterclockwise) in the plane is a linear transformation. That is, let \(T_\theta : \nR^2 \to \nR^2\) be the rotation map.

exm-shift.title: Shift Operator
exm-shift.html: Fix \(\theta \in \nR\). Determine whether the shift operator \(S_\theta : C(\nR) \to C(\nR)\) defined by \(S_\theta(f)(x) = f(x - \theta)\) is a linear transformation. (This operator translates the graph of \(f\) by \(\theta\) units to the right.)

exm-squaring.title: Squaring
exm-squaring.html: Determine whether \(T : F^2 \to F^2\) defined by \(T(a_1, a_2) = (a_1^2, 0)\) is a linear transformation.

exm-trace-kernel-image.title: Trace
exm-trace-kernel-image.html: Let \(\tr : M_2(\nR) \to \nR\) be defined by \(\tr(\A) = a_{11} + a_{22}\). Find the kernel and image of \(\tr\).

exm-trace-matrices.title: Trace
exm-trace-matrices.html: Determine whether the trace function \(\tr : M_n(F) \to F\) defined by \(\tr(\A) = \sum_{i=1}^n a_{ii}\) is a linear transformation.

exm-translation.title: Translation
exm-translation.html: Determine whether \(T : \nR^2 \to \nR^2\) defined by \(T(\v) = \v + \mathbf{c}\) for some fixed nonzero \(\mathbf{c} \in \nR^2\) is a linear transformation.

exm-zero-map.title: Zero Map
exm-zero-map.html: For any vector spaces \(V\) and \(W\), determine whether the zero map \(0 : V \to W\) defined by \(0(\v) = \mathbf{0}_W\) for all \(\v \in V\) is a linear transformation.

thm-equivalent-condition.title: Equivalent Characterization of Linearity
thm-equivalent-condition.html: Let \(V, W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) and \(T: V \to W\) be a function. Then \(T\) is a linear transformation if and only if \[ T(\alpha \v_1 + \beta \v_2) = \alpha T(\v_1) + \beta T(\v_2) \] for all \(\alpha, \beta \in F\) and \(\v_1, \v_2 \in V\).

thm-linear-combination.title: Linear Maps Preserve Linear Combinations
thm-linear-combination.html: Let \(T: V \to W\) be a linear transformation. Then for any vectors \(\v_1, \ldots, \v_n \in V\) and scalars \(a_1, \ldots, a_n \in F\): \[ T\left( \sum_{i=1}^n a_i \v_i \right) = \sum_{i=1}^n a_i T(\v_i). \]

thm-linear-transform-basis.title: Linear Transformations are Determined by Their Action on a Basis
thm-linear-transform-basis.title_html: Linear Transformations are Determined by Their Action on a Basis
thm-linear-transform-basis.html:
Let \(T: V \to W\) be a linear transformation and \(V\) is finite dimensional, and \(B = \{ \v_1, \dots, \v_n \}\) be a basis for \(V\). Then we have:

  1. For every \(\v \in V\), \(f(\v)\) is a linear combination of \(f(\v_1), f(\v_2), \dots, f(\v_n)\).
  2. Suppose the linear transformation \(g : V \to W\) satisfies \(g(\v_i) = f(\v_i)\) for all \(i\). Then \(g = f\).

We say ‘\(f\) is determined by \(f(\v_1), \dots, f(\v_n)\)’ in this case.

thm-preserves-negation.title: Linear Maps Preserve Negation
thm-preserves-negation.html: Let \(T: V \to W\) be a linear transformation. Then \(T(-\v) = -T(\v)\) for all \(\v \in V\).

thm-prop-image.title: Properties of Image
thm-prop-image.html:
Let \(f: V \to W\) be a linear transformation. Then:

  1. \(\im (f)\) is a subspace of \(W\);

  2. \(f\) is surjective iff \(\im (f) = W\).

thm-prop-kernel.title: Properties of Kernel
thm-prop-kernel.html:
Let \(f: V \to W\) be a linear transformation. Then:

  1. \(\ker (f)\) is a subspace of \(V\);

  2. \(f\) is injective iff \(\ker (f) = \left\{ \mathbf{0}_V \right\}\).

thm-rank-nullity.title: Rank-Nullity Theorem
thm-rank-nullity.html: Let \(V\) be a finite dimensional vector space and \(f : V \to W\) be a linear transformation. Then we have \[ \nullity(f) + \rank(f) = \dim (V). \]

thm-zero-maps-to-zero.title: Zero Maps to Zero
thm-zero-maps-to-zero.html: Let \(T: V \to W\) be a linear transformation. Then \(T(\mathbf{0}_V) = \mathbf{0}_W\).
